verdicts.reasoning:
Reproduced on a clean `git archive HEAD` snapshot (2093fed). The live working tree is being edited at the same time (uncommitted changes to compute_limits.js, export_targets.js, figure.js and limits.json), so every check below ran on the snapshot. Scripts: scratchpad/review1/v/f1.js and f1b.js.

compute_limits.js:62 stores `S1*f*f`. I drew the median soldier at the stored f with the arms at the rest angle (the pose the limit card draws), then read it with the page's own measureSheet (1,060 kg/m³, 7.5% fat, 2,000 px):
- arms, f=1.2539: 40.51 (stored 42.42)
- thighs, f=1.3464: 45.89 (stored 48.91)
- face, f=2.837: 191.95 at 1,600 px (stored 217.14)

The other templates overstate the same way. Face-limit shapes measure 161.5–202.2 (stored 180.6–233.3). The ratio f²/measured runs 1.04–1.09 for arms and thighs and 1.10–1.14 for face. Coleman's f<1 arms value goes the other way (0.96).

The page's own target tool agrees: asked for 42.42 on the median soldier, it answers "× 1.28: it measures 42". The stored arms limit uses × 1.254.

The method text ("that shape's score is read with the measuring tool") is therefore not what the code does.

Knock-on effects on HEAD:
- The arms headline 42.42 sits above HUMAN_TOP 41.50 ("no real man on this chart scores above 42"). Measured, it is 40.5, below.
- The face band top of 233 makes the last gap say "The hands to face limit lies somewhere from 86 to 230, reaching into the bottom of this stretch". Measured, the top is about 202, below Ollie's 216.
- The face definition text "contact geometry alone ... puts it near 220" should read about 190.

Corrections to the finding:
- HEAD gap 1 is "Score 45 to 62" and lists only the thighs limit. The arms note sits under the "Score 32 to 45" band. The quoted "Two limits ..." text is not on HEAD.
- The pessimistic bound at f=1.786 measures 86.54, close to the stored 86.06, so that part changes little.
- The measured value depends on the arm pose (face shape at 20°: 152.6; at rest: 191.9). The fix must fix the pose.

Reproduced in the rendered HEAD page (scratchpad/review1/v/f2.js). I ran Figure.armRestAngle and thighContact on figureOf's own chart figures (Figure.human at each build's height and girths).

The reviewer's numbers match exactly: Coleman 39.4° and 1.00, Big Ramy 39.7° and 1.00, Eddie Hall 35.1° and 0.82, Kingpin 34.9° and 0.84.

The problem goes further than reported. Several chart figures meet the 30° arms test well below the arms band (37–43):
- Arnold (score 27.5): 31.5°
- Bane (30.0): 34.1°
- Sergio Oliva (31.1): 33.4°
- Hafthor (33.8): 30.3°
- Lasha (34.8): 32.3°
- Phil Heath (35.7): 34.7°
- Dorian Yates (36.3): 36.7°

Luke Cage (41.1) also has thighs touching to the knee.

The page says otherwise:
- Under the "Score 32 to 45" band, the note above Coleman, Ramy and Kingpin reads "LIMIT · ARMS OUT · ABOUT 42 (37–43 across six template shapes)".
- Gap 1 (45–62) says "A limit of the drawn body falls in this stretch: thighs touch all the way to the knee (about 49)". The band is 42–53.
- Coleman's own drawer shows his thighs merged to the knee (coleman_drawer.png) at 39.

The cause is the footing. Template limits are scored from drawn volume: Coleman's template S(f=1) is 44.94 against his chart score of 39.16. The page's own drawer admits "The drawing shows the build; the score uses the weight". The limits section and the gap copy never say so.

The gap-copy quote in the finding ("Score 42 to 62 ... Two limits") does not match HEAD's wording. The contradiction itself is on the page.
verdicts.better_fix:
Make the page say what its own figures show, and put the limits on one footing:
1. In compute_limits.js (or the page), test every chart build's own figure:
   - arms: `Fig.armRestAngle(d => Fig.human(T, e.height.value, g, {}, {buttockFit, armDeg: d})) >= 30`
   - thighs: `Fig.thighContact(fig) >= 1`
   Store the results as `met_by`.
2. Add to the limit note and gap copy, for example: "The chart's own outlines already meet this test from Arnold Schwarzenegger (28) up (arms) / Ronnie Coleman (39) up (thighs). These limit scores come from the widened template's drawn volume, and the chart's scores come from weight: Coleman's drawing reads about 45 against his 39."
3. Add the same caveat to settings.limits.notes.
4. Optionally rescale each template's limits by chart score / S(f=1). Drawing chart figures at max(20, rest angle) is a separate cosmetic choice.

verdicts.reasoning:
Reproduced in the rendered HEAD page (f3.js; the input hint is "15 to 900"):
- median soldier: 217 gives "× 3.22: it measures 200 (target 220)"; 600 gives 580; 900 gives 760
- Coleman: 217 gives 210; 600 gives 450; 900 gives 590

I measured those sheets in Node with the page's own settings (f3b.js):
- median soldier: f=7 and f=7.17 are rejected (ok=false)
- Coleman: f=4, 4.93 and 6.66 are rejected
Each fails "view heights agree within 2%" (5–26% spread) and the side-neck check.

Cause: the front outline's top rises above the 1.80 m skull (Coleman f=4.93: 2.053 m; median soldier f=7.17: 1.901 m). That happens because deltR scales with f. heightRef 'top' then shrinks the scale, so the score grows slower than f².

The page never shows r.ok or the errors. The CLI on HEAD, `export_targets.js --score 900`, prints "widths x 7.328 ... measured score 770.0 (target 900); checks: FAIL view heights ...; FAIL side-view neck ..." and still writes the three PNGs. `--score 600 --build ronnie_coleman` gives 561.4 with the same FAILs (output in scratchpad/review1/v/tgt).

Even reachable targets miss: 217 gives 200–205, because there is only one sqrt correction.

BRIEF.md:56 asks to "export the outline for any target score" for gap fillers, which need 216–924.

I checked the root-cause fix (f3c.js). Measuring with the skull row taken from the rendered sheet (row = ground − H·k) brings median-soldier f=7.17 to 896.6 and Coleman f=4.93 to 666.7, both ok=true.
verdicts.better_fix:
1. Measure target sheets with heightRef 'skull' and skullRows {front, side, back} = Math.round(img.ground - H*img.k). renderSheet knows ground and k. Do this in app.html scoreAt, export_targets.measureTemplate and the --sheet path.
2. Replace the one-step sqrt correction, in both places, with a bracketing bisection on the measured score:
   - double hi until score(hi) >= target or hi > 12, treating !r.ok as out of range
   - then about 20 bisection steps on log f
3. If no passing sheet reaches the target, set targetStatus to "Out of reach for this base: the largest passing outline measures X" and do not set `target` or the images.
4. In the CLI, print r.errors and exit 1 without writing when !result.ok.

verdicts.reasoning:
Reproduced on the rendered HEAD page (f4.js).

The values:
- median soldier: H 1.755, W 84.60, fat 25.3%, S 21.04, W/H³ 15.65
- 95th percentile: H 1.87, W 110.69, fat 33.9%, S 20.15, W/H³ 16.93 (8% higher)

At the median's 25.3% fat, the 95th would score 1.8 × 110.69 × 0.747 / 1.87³ = 22.76.

S divides out height cubed. The Army equation's height term (−70.041 log10 H) actually lowers his estimated fat. His lower score comes entirely from the higher fat estimate that his 113 cm waist drives.

The page sentence (settings.json:736) "The 95th scores lower than the median because he is taller, not more muscular" is wrong.
verdicts.better_fix: In settings.json stops[0].sub, replace the last sentence with: "The 95th scores lower than the median because the Army equations give his 113 cm waist much more fat (34% against 25%). At the median's body fat he would score about 23."

verdicts.reasoning:
The cited incident is real. At 3cd65f5 (first publish) and at 7f595f2, settings.limits.notes[2] ("... 49 of 50 people still managed ..., the lowest setting tested") differed from limits.json. The shipped dist contains "with the elbow held to 120°, people still manage eating, drinking and washing ...".

Two claims in the finding are wrong on HEAD (2093fed):
- limits.json now equals compute_limits.run() exactly (f5.js, 13 s).
- test/test.js:113 ("data/limits.json carries the current settings text") already checks verdict, method, notes and each item's label, short, tiny, definition and headline. So the cited text-staleness repeat would now fail the tests.

The remaining gap is real: the numbers are never checked against the generator. In a copy of HEAD I set settings.limits.arms.angle_deg = 25 and face.pessimistic_girth_factor = 1.6 without regenerating:
- `node test/test.js` reports "24 passed, 0 failed"
- limits.json still says angle 30 and steep_bmi_fit 86.06 (regenerated: 69.07)

The same happens for any change to figure.js, outline.json or builds.json that moves the limits. CI only regenerates dist.

Confirmed on HEAD. test/test.js:268-281 checks Fig.armBoneClearance (monotone, and 0 at base). Nothing in src/ or tools/ calls armBoneClearance or armClearance. compute_limits.js uses Fig.armRestAngle.

The two functions give very different values (f6.js), for f = 1, 1.2, 1.254, 1.4, 1.8:
- armBoneClearance: 0, 1.75, 6.5, 16.5, 49.5°
- armRestAngle: 8.0, 25.7, 30.6, 40.9, 69.6°

No test calls armRestAngle, elbowFlexion, solveScale or the crease calibration, or checks the stored limit scores. So the f² overstatement in F1 passes the suite.

The test's message "an ordinary man can let his arms hang" is checked with the bone-only function, not the one the page uses.

Reproduced on HEAD measure.js (f7.js). The test case is a 40 × 100 px rectangle at rows 100–199 with k = kProfile([[100,1],[200,0.5]]):
- exact and sliceRows: 94,562
- sliceRotated: 110,113 at 0.001°, 109,748 at 1°, 107,964 at 10° (+14–16%)

Cause: kf(r) gets the rotated-grid row index (half-pixel units from umin), not the image row that kProfile expects. With a constant k the two functions agree (94,248).

The bug is latent. In duo-validation.json the torso has kPoints but no angle, and the arm and leg parts have angles but constant k. So Rex's 2.545 m³ is unaffected. frontOnly's doc still lists kPoints and angle as a valid combination.

I verified the fix below: 94,562 at 0.001°, 94,312 at 1°, 93,737 at 10°, and constant-k results unchanged.
